_readme: LANDED-FIX MARKERS — read by .claude/hooks/push-clobber-gate.py before every
push to main. Each entry names a string that must appear in a file at least
`min` times in the commit being pushed. A push whose blob is missing one is
blocked, because that is exactly what a rebuild-from-stale-base clobber looks
like: the Sky Lance chain fix was silently reverted TWICE in one day by
parallel commits (940557ce, 8acd2b7e) whose game file was built from a
snapshot read before the fix landed. Nothing conflicted, nothing failed —
ADD an entry whenever you land a fix in a hot file via a rebuild pipeline:
pick a string unique to your change (a function name you introduced beats a
comment phrase) and set `min` to its count in your shipped blob.
REMOVE an entry only in a TWO-STEP dance: first push a manifest-only commit
deleting the entry (the gate unions this file across the pushed commit AND
origin/main, so removing the entry and the code in one push is blocked —
deliberately, because a stale rebuild produces that same shape); then push
the code change. If the gate blocks you and you did NOT intend to remove
that fix: git fetch origin and rebuild your file from the CURRENT tip.
